PR_readback.title: fix: drain lifecycle sinks before engine and worker teardown
PR_readback.body:
Registered lifecycle sinks currently have no normal shutdown callback. EngineCore and TP processes can exit before an exporter writes its bounded final summary, leaving already delivered request records without loss-free close evidence. Add an optional generic `EventBus.close_sinks` and call it after each busy loop ends, before EngineCore model-worker teardown and WorkerWrapperBase extension/device teardown. Emit-only sinks remain valid; actual close results and exceptions are retained without manufacturing a success record. Host imports no specific MOD.

This branch preserves the exact experimental commit `f67ad57c854940a90ddfa82a4a984bb6ce2ff923`, based on compatible Host772. A three-way integration against main `5bc5ad2cbfbf23258cfedbeb48cb42760fda9e39` applies cleanly and changes only the three production paths; it does not replace main with the old Host tree. Please use a merge commit, preserving the experimental commit as an ancestor. The experiment continues to select that exact source and its already built wheel; merging does not substitute main as its runtime.

Validation: nine portable CPU source contracts passed in0.14s against the prospective merged production files. They execute the real pure EventBus and actual shutdown method bodies, covering detach-before-close, legacy emit-only sinks, close/property errors, and engine/worker ordering despite teardown failures. They require pytest only, do not import Profiler or model/device modules, and have a dedicated CPU workflow. Run `python -m pytest -q --confcutdir=tests/plugins tests/plugins/test_event_bus_shutdown.py`.

The original exact experimental source also built an official empty wheel; all3354 package members,2701 Python files and RECORD were verified against its exact Git/SCM source. This is build/source evidence, not a new native qualification. A real sink needs a finite parent grace period; explicit timeout0 is unchanged. The separate H2 run uses the supported five-second parent budget for the original two-second exporter closes. Slow callbacks, crashes and forced kills can still leave close unknown. No summary is synthesized, and previous failed/missing-summary evidence is retained.

No open same-branch/lifecycle-drain PR was found in the recorded canonical-repository check. Prepared with AI assistance; changed lines and the exact merge ancestry remain subject to the submitting reviewer's review. This affects shutdown instrumentation rather than model algorithms; no new model-quality or formal performance result is claimed here.

+## Kernel breakdown
+
+Add `--profile-dir DIR` to see where the time goes. After timing, each case is
+replayed 3 more times under `torch.profiler`; every rank writes
+`DIR/<case>.rank<r>.kernels.json` (GPU time per kernel per forward, sorted)
+and `DIR/<case>.rank<r>.trace.json.gz` (open in Perfetto). Rank 0's top
+kernels are printed and included in `--output-json`.
+
+```bash
+python -m vllm.benchmarks.forward.profile DIR/decode.rank0.kernels.json
+# Before/after a change, same case: per-kernel deltas, largest first.
+python -m vllm.benchmarks.forward.profile base/decode.rank0.kernels.json new/decode.rank0.kernels.json
+```
+
+- Kernels are grouped by name without template or function arguments; the
+  JSON keeps one full name per group in `example`.
+- Only the timed forward is included: the in-graph KV restore and rank
+  rendezvous are excluded (`pre_forward_us`). `span_us` (first to last
+  forward kernel) should be close to `median_us`, a bit higher from profiler
+  overhead; `busy_us` can exceed it when streams overlap.
+- Compare the same rank across runs: under EP, ranks differ (e.g. collective
+  wait time shows up inside communication kernels).
+
+For Nsight Systems (NVTX, NCCL, CPU side, GPU metrics), skip `--profile-dir`:
+the two can't share CUPTI. Each case's 3 profiled replays run between
+`cudaProfilerStart`/`Stop` in an NVTX range `forward/<case>`, so a capture range
+records only them, one report per case (and rank):
+
+```bash
+nsys profile --capture-range=cudaProfilerApi --capture-range-end=repeat \
+  --cuda-graph-trace=node -o prof vllm bench forward ...       # prof.1, prof.2, ...
+torchrun --nproc-per-node=4 --no-python nsys profile ... -o prof_rank%q{RANK} \
+  python -m vllm.entrypoints.cli.main bench forward ...
+nsys stats --report cuda_gpu_kern_sum --format csv -o kern prof.1.nsys-rep
+```
+
+Keep `--capture-range-end=repeat`: nsys's default stops after the first case
+and leaves the bench hanging. `nsys stats` also counts the KV restore copies
+that the JSON summary excludes.

 Upstream configs are `@strict` dataclasses. Checkpoint keys upstream does not
-declare survive as plain attributes. Defaults that only vLLM sets, and values

 | Hazard | Signal | Fix |
 | --- | --- | --- |
 | Upstream consumes legacy keys | `__post_init__` pops keys the model reads (`deepseek_v4` `compress_ratios`) | Read the upstream replacement (`layer_types`, `mlp_layer_types`, per-layer `rope_parameters`) |
 | Renamed or dropped fields | Diff shows `<MISSING>` for a field the model reads | Read the upstream name; derive dropped flags from what implies them (`enable_moe_block` from `num_experts`) |

 | Type check on the config | `ctx.get_hf_config(SomeConfig)` relies on the vendored base class | Accept the upstream class too, e.g. a `Cosmos3ProcessingInfo` overriding `get_hf_config` |
 | Remote code takes over | Checkpoint `config.json` has `auto_map`; with `--trust-remote-code`, the hub class replaces the native one once vLLM stops registering its own | Check the remote class loads; if not, register the upstream class for that `model_type` |

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+#
+# Derive everything the release pipeline needs about a ROCm stack from its base
+# Dockerfile, so the stack's image is the single input to every ROCm script.
+#
+# Usage: source .buildkite/scripts/rocm/stack.sh <base-dockerfile>
+#   e.g. docker/Dockerfile.rocm_base (ROCm 10.0) or docker/Dockerfile.rocm_72_base
+#
+# Exports:
+#   ROCM_STACK_BASE_DOCKERFILE  the base Dockerfile
+#   ROCM_STACK_DOCKERFILE       the matching vLLM Dockerfile (base name minus _base)
+#   ROCM_STACK_THEROCK          1 if the ROCm SDK comes from TheRock wheels
+#   ROCM_STACK_VERSION          ROCm version, e.g. 10.0.0 or 7.2.3
+#   ROCM_STACK_VARIANT          wheel variant and Docker Hub tag flavor from major.minor,
+#                               same rule as setup.py (rocm100, rocm72)
+#   ROCM_STACK_IMAGE_KEY        hash of the base Dockerfile (base image cache key)
+#   ROCM_STACK_WHEEL_KEY        hash of the base Dockerfile plus files it COPYs from
+#                               the repo (base wheel cache key)
+#   ROCM_STACK_ECR_BASE         ECR tag of the cached base image
+#   ROCM_STACK_ECR_IMAGE        ECR tag of this commit's release image
+#   ROCM_STACK_BASE_WHEELS_DIR  local dir for base wheels (also the artifact path)
+#   ROCM_STACK_VLLM_WHEEL_DIR   local dir for the vLLM wheel (also the artifact path)
+
+rocm_stack_init() {
+    local base="$1"
+    if [[ ! -f "$base" ]]; then
+        echo "ROCm base Dockerfile not found: $base" >&2
+        return 2
+    fi
+    ROCM_STACK_BASE_DOCKERFILE="$base"
+    ROCM_STACK_DOCKERFILE="${base%_base}"
+
+    local sdk
+    sdk=$(sed -nE 's/^ARG ROCM_SDK_VERSION=([0-9.]+).*/\1/p' "$base" | head -1)
+    if [[ -n "$sdk" ]]; then
+        ROCM_STACK_THEROCK=1
+        ROCM_STACK_VERSION="$sdk"
+    else
+        ROCM_STACK_THEROCK=0
+        # BASE_IMAGE format: rocm/dev-ubuntu-22.04:7.2.3-complete -> 7.2.3
+        ROCM_STACK_VERSION=$(sed -nE 's/^ARG BASE_IMAGE=.*:([0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)+).*/\1/p' "$base" | head -1)
+    fi
+    if [[ -z "$ROCM_STACK_VERSION" ]]; then
+        echo "Could not determine the ROCm version from $base" >&2
+        return 2
+    fi
+
+    local major minor
+    IFS=. read -r major minor _ <<< "$ROCM_STACK_VERSION"
+    ROCM_STACK_VARIANT="rocm${major}${minor}"
+
+    ROCM_STACK_IMAGE_KEY=$(sha256sum "$base" | cut -c1-16)
+    local inputs
+    inputs=$(grep -E '^COPY ' "$base" | grep -v -- '--from' | awk '{print $2}' || true)
+    if [[ -z "$inputs" ]]; then
+        ROCM_STACK_WHEEL_KEY="$ROCM_STACK_IMAGE_KEY"
+    else
+        # shellcheck disable=SC2086
+        ROCM_STACK_WHEEL_KEY=$(sha256sum "$base" $inputs | sha256sum | cut -c1-16)
+    fi
+
+    local ecr="public.ecr.aws/q9t5s3a7/vllm-release-repo"
+    ROCM_STACK_ECR_BASE="${ecr}:${ROCM_STACK_IMAGE_KEY}-${ROCM_STACK_VARIANT}-base"
+    ROCM_STACK_ECR_IMAGE="${ecr}:${BUILDKITE_COMMIT:-unknown}-${ROCM_STACK_VARIANT}"
+    ROCM_STACK_BASE_WHEELS_DIR="artifacts/${ROCM_STACK_VARIANT}-base-wheels"
+    ROCM_STACK_VLLM_WHEEL_DIR="artifacts/${ROCM_STACK_VARIANT}-vllm-wheel"
+
+    export ROCM_STACK_BASE_DOCKERFILE ROCM_STACK_DOCKERFILE ROCM_STACK_THEROCK \
+        ROCM_STACK_VERSION ROCM_STACK_VARIANT ROCM_STACK_IMAGE_KEY \
+        ROCM_STACK_WHEEL_KEY ROCM_STACK_ECR_BASE ROCM_STACK_ECR_IMAGE \
+        ROCM_STACK_BASE_WHEELS_DIR ROCM_STACK_VLLM_WHEEL_DIR
+}
+
+if [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; then
+    rocm_stack_init "$1"

+name: Recipes

+# Validate recipe changes against the renderer that publishes them
+# (recipes.vllm.ai). The check logic lives in vllm-project/recipes and tracks
+# its main branch, so a PR is held to the same validation that runs when
+# vllm-project/recipes picks up this directory after merge.
+
+on:
+  pull_request:
+    paths:
+      - 'recipes/**'
+      - '.github/workflows/recipes.yml'
+
+concurrency:
+  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
+  cancel-in-progress: true
+
+permissions:
+  contents: read
+
+jobs:
+  validate:
+    name: Recipes
+    if: github.repository_owner == 'vllm-project'
+    uses: vllm-project/recipes/.github/workflows/validate-recipes.yml@main
+    with:
+      source: vllm
+      path: recipes

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Benchmark the fused Muse-Spark QK-norm + RoPE + KV-insert kernel vs unfused.
+
+``tuned_us`` forces the cp.async schedule ``fused_qk_norm_rope`` only auto-selects
+on SM 9.0; ``unfused_us`` is what production runs.
+"""
+
+import argparse
+import itertools
+
+import torch
+
+import vllm._custom_ops as ops
+
+HEAD_DIM = 64
+DEFAULT_TOKENS = [1, 8, 64, 256, 1024, 4096, 8192, 16384, 32768, 65536]
+
+
+def make_cos_sin_cache(max_pos, rotary_dim, base, device):
+    inv_freq = 1.0 / (
+        base
+        ** (
+            torch.arange(0, rotary_dim, 2, dtype=torch.float32, device=device)
+            / rotary_dim
+        )
+    )
+    t = torch.arange(max_pos, dtype=torch.float32, device=device)
+    freqs = torch.einsum("i,j->ij", t, inv_freq)
+    return torch.cat((freqs.cos(), freqs.sin()), dim=-1)
+
+
+class Case:
+    """Everything a single (num_tokens, config) measurement needs."""
+
+    def __init__(self, num_tokens, nq, nkv, dtype, kv_cache_dtype, device):
+        self.num_tokens = num_tokens
+        self.nq, self.nkv = nq, nkv
+        self.dtype = dtype
+        self.kv_cache_dtype = kv_cache_dtype
+        self.eps = 1e-5
+        self.block_size = 128
+        self.rotary_dim = HEAD_DIM
+
+        self.qsz, self.kvsz = nq * HEAD_DIM, nkv * HEAD_DIM
+        self.row = self.qsz + 2 * self.kvsz + self.qsz  # [q | k | v | o_gate]
+        self.qkv = torch.randn(num_tokens, self.row, dtype=dtype, device=device)
+        self.pristine = self.qkv.clone()
+
+        max_pos = 32768
+        self.cos_sin = make_cos_sin_cache(max_pos, self.rotary_dim, 500_000.0, device)
+        self.positions = torch.randint(
+            0, max_pos, (num_tokens,), dtype=torch.int64, device=device
+        )
+
+        num_blocks = (num_tokens + self.block_size - 1) // self.block_size + 1
+        storage = torch.uint8 if kv_cache_dtype != "auto" else dtype
+        self.kv_cache = torch.zeros(
+            num_blocks,
+            nkv,
+            self.block_size,
+            2 * HEAD_DIM,
+            dtype=storage,
+            device=device,
+        )
+        self.k_cache, self.v_cache = self.kv_cache.transpose(1, 2).split(
+            HEAD_DIM, dim=-1
+        )
+        self.slot_mapping = torch.randperm(
+            num_blocks * self.block_size, dtype=torch.int64, device=device
+        )[:num_tokens]
+        self.k_scale = torch.tensor(1.0, dtype=torch.float32, device=device)
+        self.v_scale = torch.tensor(1.0, dtype=torch.float32, device=device)
+        self.ones = torch.ones(HEAD_DIM, dtype=dtype, device=device)
+        self.q_fp8 = torch.empty(
+            num_tokens, self.qsz, dtype=torch.float8_e4m3fn, device=device
+        )
+        self.q_scale = torch.tensor(0.37, dtype=torch.float32, device=device)
+
+    def views(self):
+        q, k, v, _ = self.qkv.split([self.qsz, self.kvsz, self.kvsz, self.qsz], dim=-1)
+        return q, k, v
+
+    def fused(self, use_rope=True, quant_query=False):
+        ops.fused_muse_spark_qknorm_rope_kv_insert(
+            self.qkv,
+            self.positions,
+            self.nq,
+            self.nkv,
+            HEAD_DIM,
+            self.eps,
+            cos_sin_cache=self.cos_sin if use_rope else None,
+            rotary_dim=self.rotary_dim if use_rope else 0,
+            slot_mapping=self.slot_mapping,
+            kv_cache=self.kv_cache,
+            block_size=self.block_size,
+            kv_cache_dtype=self.kv_cache_dtype,
+            k_scale=self.k_scale if self.kv_cache_dtype != "auto" else None,
+            v_scale=self.v_scale if self.kv_cache_dtype != "auto" else None,
+            q_fp8_out=self.q_fp8 if quant_query else None,
+            q_scale=self.q_scale if quant_query else None,
+        )
+
+    def separate_query_quant(self, use_rope=True):
+        self.fused(use_rope)
+        ops.scaled_fp8_quant(self.qkv[:, : self.qsz], scale=self.q_scale)
+
+    def _insert(self):
+        _, k, v = self.views()
+        ops.reshape_and_cache_flash(
+            k.view(-1, self.nkv, HEAD_DIM),
+            v.view(-1, self.nkv, HEAD_DIM),
+            self.k_cache,
+            self.v_cache,
+            self.slot_mapping,
+            self.kv_cache_dtype,
+            self.k_scale,
+            self.v_scale,
+        )
+
+    def unfused_rope(self, token_heads_per_warp: int = -1):
+        ops.fused_qk_norm_rope(
+            self.qkv,
+            self.nq,
+            self.nkv,
+            self.nkv + self.nq,  # v heads plus the o-gate
+            HEAD_DIM,
+            self.eps,
+            self.ones,
+            self.ones,
+            self.cos_sin,
+            False,
+            self.positions,
+            token_heads_per_warp,
+        )
+        self._insert()
+
+    def fused_bytes(self):
+        el = self.qkv.element_size()
+        cache_el = self.kv_cache.element_size()
+        read = (self.nq + 2 * self.nkv) * HEAD_DIM * el
+        write = (self.nq + self.nkv) * HEAD_DIM * el
+        cache = 2 * self.nkv * HEAD_DIM * cache_el
+        return self.num_tokens * (read + write + cache)
+
+
+def _l2_bytes(device) -> int:
+    return torch.cuda.get_device_properties(device).L2_cache_size
+
+
+def _peak_bandwidth(device) -> float:
+    """Measured large-copy bandwidth, in GB/s -- the practical ceiling."""
+    n = 1 << 28  # 256 Mi elements = 512 MiB each way at 2 bytes
+    a = torch.empty(n, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device=device)
+    b = torch.empty_like(a)
+    for _ in range(3):
+        b.copy_(a)
+    torch.accelerator.synchronize()
+    start, end = torch.cuda.Event(True), torch.cuda.Event(True)
+    start.record()
+    iters = 20
+    for _ in range(iters):
+        b.copy_(a)
+    end.record()
+    torch.accelerator.synchronize()
+    ms = start.elapsed_time(end) / iters
+    return (2 * a.numel() * a.element_size()) / (ms * 1e-3) / 1e9
+
+
+def time_eager(fn, warmup=20, iters=100) -> float:
+    for _ in range(warmup):
+        fn()
+    torch.accelerator.synchronize()
+    start, end = torch.cuda.Event(True), torch.cuda.Event(True)
+    start.record()
+    for _ in range(iters):
+        fn()
+    end.record()
+    torch.accelerator.synchronize()
+    return start.elapsed_time(end) / iters * 1e3  # us
+
+
+def time_graph(fn, warmup=10, iters=50, inner=32) -> float:
+    """GPU time per call; ``inner`` calls per graph amortize the ~2 us replay."""
+    side = torch.cuda.Stream()
+    side.wait_stream(torch.cuda.current_stream())
+    with torch.cuda.stream(side):
+        for _ in range(warmup):
+            fn()
+    torch.cuda.current_stream().wait_stream(side)
+    graph = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
+    with torch.cuda.graph(graph):
+        for _ in range(inner):
+            fn()
+    for _ in range(3):
+        graph.replay()
+    torch.accelerator.synchronize()
+    start, end = torch.cuda.Event(True), torch.cuda.Event(True)
+    start.record()
+    for _ in range(iters):
+        graph.replay()
+    end.record()
+    torch.accelerator.synchronize()
+    return start.elapsed_time(end) / (iters * inner) * 1e3  # us
+
+
+def main():
+    p = argparse.ArgumentParser()
+    p.add_argument("--nq", type=int, default=32, help="query heads per rank")
+    p.add_argument("--nkv", type=int, default=4, help="kv heads per rank")
+    p.add_argument("--kv-cache-dtype", default="auto", choices=["auto", "fp8"])
+    p.add_argument("--dtype", default="bfloat16", choices=["bfloat16", "float16"])
+    p.add_argument("--tokens", type=int, nargs="*", default=DEFAULT_TOKENS)
+    p.add_argument("--csv", default=None)
+    p.add_argument("--no-graph", action="store_true")
+    p.add_argument(
+        "--query-fp8", action="store_true", help="compare fused Q quantization"
+    )
+    args = p.parse_args()
+
+    device = "cuda"
+    dtype = getattr(torch, args.dtype)
+    if args.query_fp8:
+        if args.kv_cache_dtype != "fp8":
+            p.error("--query-fp8 requires --kv-cache-dtype fp8")
+        timer = time_eager if args.no_graph else time_graph
+        print(f"device: {torch.cuda.get_device_name()}; nq={args.nq}, nkv={args.nkv}")
+        print("layer,tokens,separate_us,fused_us,speedup")
+        rows = []
+        for use_rope, nt in itertools.product([True, False], args.tokens):
+            case = Case(nt, args.nq, args.nkv, dtype, args.kv_cache_dtype, device)
+            separate_us = timer(lambda c=case, r=use_rope: c.separate_query_quant(r))
+            case.qkv.copy_(case.pristine)
+            fused_us = timer(lambda c=case, r=use_rope: c.fused(r, quant_query=True))
+            row = (
+                "rope" if use_rope else "nope",
+                nt,
+                separate_us,
+                fused_us,
+                separate_us / fused_us,
+            )
+            rows.append(row)
+            print(f"{row[0]},{nt},{separate_us:.3f},{fused_us:.3f},{row[4]:.3f}")
+        if args.csv:
+            import csv
+
+            with open(args.csv, "w", newline="") as f:
+                writer = csv.writer(f)
+                writer.writerow(
+                    ["layer", "tokens", "separate_us", "fused_us", "speedup"]
+                )
+                writer.writerows(rows)
+        return
+    peak = _peak_bandwidth(device)
+    print(
+        f"device: {torch.cuda.get_device_name()}   measured copy peak: {peak:.0f} GB/s"
+    )
+    print(
+        f"config: nq={args.nq} nkv={args.nkv} head_dim={HEAD_DIM} "
+        f"dtype={args.dtype} kv_cache={args.kv_cache_dtype}\n"
+    )
+
+    modes = ["rope"]
+    l2 = _l2_bytes(device)
+    print(
+        f"rows marked * have a working set inside the {l2 / 2**20:.0f} MiB L2, "
+        "so their bandwidth is not an HBM number\n"
+    )
+    header = (
+        f"{'layer':>5} {'tokens':>7} {'fused_us':>9} {'unfused_us':>11} "
+        f"{'tuned_us':>9} {'speedup':>8} {'GB/s':>8} {'SOL%':>6}"
+    )
+    rows = []
+    for mode, use_graph in itertools.product(modes, [False, True]):
+        if use_graph and args.no_graph:
+            continue
+        label = "graph" if use_graph else "eager"
+        print(f"── {mode} layer, {label} ──")
+        print(header)
+        timer = time_graph if use_graph else time_eager
+        for nt in args.tokens:
+            case = Case(nt, args.nq, args.nkv, dtype, args.kv_cache_dtype, device)
+            use_rope = mode == "rope"
+            fused_us = timer(lambda c=case, r=use_rope: c.fused(r))
+            baseline = case.unfused_rope
+            unfused_us = timer(baseline)
+            tuned_us = (
+                min(timer(lambda c=case, t=t: c.unfused_rope(t)) for t in (4, 8))
+                if use_rope
+                else unfused_us
+            )
+            nbytes = case.fused_bytes()
+            gbps = nbytes / (fused_us * 1e-6) / 1e9
+            sol = 100.0 * gbps / peak
+            resident = "*" if nbytes < l2 else " "
+            print(
+                f"{mode:>5} {nt:>7} {fused_us:>9.2f} {unfused_us:>11.2f} "
+                f"{tuned_us:>9.2f} {tuned_us / fused_us:>7.2f}x {gbps:>8.0f} "
+                f"{sol:>5.1f}%{resident}"
+            )
+            rows.append((mode, label, nt, fused_us, unfused_us, tuned_us, gbps, sol))
+        print()
+
+    if args.csv:
+        import csv
+
+        with open(args.csv, "w", newline="") as f:
+            w = csv.writer(f)
+            w.writerow(
+                [
+                    "layer",
+                    "timing",
+                    "tokens",
+                    "fused_us",
+                    "unfused_us",
+                    "tuned_us",
+                    "gbps",
+                    "sol",
+                ]
+            )
+            w.writerows(rows)
+        print(f"wrote {args.csv}")
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()

+ARG BASE_IMAGE=rocm/dev-ubuntu-22.04:7.2.3-complete
+ARG TRITON_BRANCH="669b31a" # release/internal/3.8.x as of 09/17
+ARG TRITON_REPO="https://github.com/ROCm/triton.git"
+ARG PYTORCH_BRANCH="733fca1" # release/2.13 as of 09/17
+ARG PYTORCH_REPO="https://github.com/ROCm/pytorch.git"
+ARG PYTORCH_VISION_BRANCH="v0.28.0"
+ARG PYTORCH_VISION_REPO="https://github.com/pytorch/vision.git"
+ARG PYTORCH_AUDIO_BRANCH="v2.11.0"
+ARG PYTORCH_AUDIO_REPO="https://github.com/pytorch/audio.git"
+ARG FA_BRANCH="0e60e394"
+ARG FA_REPO="https://github.com/Dao-AILab/flash-attention.git"
+ARG AITER_BRANCH="v0.1.25"
+ARG AITER_REPO="https://github.com/ROCm/aiter.git"
+ARG MORI_BRANCH="v1.2.3.post1"
+ARG MORI_REPO="https://github.com/ROCm/mori.git"
+ARG ROCM_SYSTEMS_REPO="https://github.com/ROCm/rocm-systems.git"
+ARG ROCPROFILER_SDK_COMMIT="2b22ab0195cc1461cd9abf3b969e9dd7c10af350"
+ARG ROCM_RUNTIME_COMMIT="af70edc91f1dc5d228fd4c076df99e65e49c4521"
+
+# Sccache configuration (only used in release pipeline)
+ARG USE_SCCACHE
+ARG SCCACHE_DOWNLOAD_URL
+ARG SCCACHE_ENDPOINT
+ARG SCCACHE_BUCKET_NAME=vllm-build-sccache
+ARG SCCACHE_REGION_NAME=us-west-2
+ARG SCCACHE_S3_NO_CREDENTIALS=0
+
+
+FROM ${BASE_IMAGE} AS base
+
+ENV PATH=/opt/rocm/llvm/bin:/opt/rocm/bin:/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin
+ENV ROCM_PATH=/opt/rocm
+ENV LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/opt/rocm/lib:/usr/local/lib:
+
+ARG PYTORCH_ROCM_ARCH=gfx90a;gfx942;gfx950;gfx1100;gfx1101;gfx1200;gfx1201;gfx1150;gfx1151
+ENV PYTORCH_ROCM_ARCH=${PYTORCH_ROCM_ARCH}
+ENV AITER_ROCM_ARCH=gfx942;gfx950
+# Note: Do not set MORI_GPU_ARCHS here, it is automatically inferred at runtime
+
+# Required for RCCL in ROCm7.1
+ENV HSA_NO_SCRATCH_RECLAIM=1
+
+ARG PYTHON_VERSION=3.12
+ENV PYTHON_VERSION=${PYTHON_VERSION}
+
+RUN mkdir -p /app
+WORKDIR /app
+ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive
+
+# Install Python and other dependencies (plus gcc-13, selected later in build_pytorch).
+RUN apt-get update -y \
+    && apt-get install -y software-properties-common git curl sudo vim less libgfortran5 libopenmpi-dev libpci-dev liblzma-dev pkg-config \
+    && for i in 1 2 3; do \
+        add-apt-repository -y ppa:deadsnakes/ppa && add-apt-repository -y ppa:ubuntu-toolchain-r/test && break || \
+        { echo "Attempt $i failed, retrying in 5s..."; sleep 5; }; \
+    done \
+    && apt-get update -y \
+    && apt-get install -y python${PYTHON_VERSION} python${PYTHON_VERSION}-dev python${PYTHON_VERSION}-venv \
+       python${PYTHON_VERSION}-lib2to3 python-is-python3 gcc-13 g++-13 \
+    && update-alternatives --install /usr/bin/python3 python3 /usr/bin/python${PYTHON_VERSION} 1 \
+    && update-alternatives --set python3 /usr/bin/python${PYTHON_VERSION} \
+    && ln -sf /usr/bin/python${PYTHON_VERSION}-config /usr/bin/python3-config \
+    && curl -sS https://bootstrap.pypa.io/get-pip.py | python${PYTHON_VERSION} \
+    && python3 --version && python3 -m pip --version
+
+RUN pip install -U packaging 'cmake<4' ninja wheel 'setuptools<80' 'pybind11<3.1.0' Cython
+RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y libjpeg-dev libsox-dev libsox-fmt-all sox && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
+
+# Install sccache if USE_SCCACHE is enabled (for release builds)
+ARG USE_SCCACHE
+ARG SCCACHE_DOWNLOAD_URL
+ARG SCCACHE_ENDPOINT
+ARG SCCACHE_BUCKET_NAME
+ARG SCCACHE_REGION_NAME
+ARG SCCACHE_S3_NO_CREDENTIALS
+RUN if [ "$USE_SCCACHE" = "1" ]; then \
+        echo "Installing sccache..." \
+        && SCCACHE_ARCH="x86_64" \
+        && SCCACHE_VERSION="v0.8.1" \
+        && SCCACHE_DL_URL="${SCCACHE_DOWNLOAD_URL:-https://github.com/mozilla/sccache/releases/download/${SCCACHE_VERSION}/sccache-${SCCACHE_VERSION}-${SCCACHE_ARCH}-unknown-linux-musl.tar.gz}" \
+        && curl -L -o /tmp/sccache.tar.gz ${SCCACHE_DL_URL} \
+        && tar -xzf /tmp/sccache.tar.gz -C /tmp \
+        && mv /tmp/sccache-${SCCACHE_VERSION}-${SCCACHE_ARCH}-unknown-linux-musl/sccache /usr/bin/sccache \
+        && chmod +x /usr/bin/sccache \
+        && rm -rf /tmp/sccache.tar.gz /tmp/sccache-${SCCACHE_VERSION}-${SCCACHE_ARCH}-unknown-linux-musl \
+        && sccache --version; \
+    fi
+
+# Setup sccache for HIP compilation via HIP_CLANG_PATH
+# This creates wrapper scripts in a separate directory and points HIP to use them
+# This avoids modifying the original ROCm binaries which can break detection
+# NOTE: HIP_CLANG_PATH is NOT set as ENV to avoid affecting downstream images (Dockerfile.rocm_72)
+# Instead, each build stage should export HIP_CLANG_PATH=/opt/sccache-wrappers if USE_SCCACHE=1
+RUN if [ "$USE_SCCACHE" = "1" ]; then \
+        echo "Setting up sccache wrappers for HIP compilation..." \
+        && mkdir -p /opt/sccache-wrappers \
+        && printf '#!/bin/bash\nexec sccache /opt/rocm/lib/llvm/bin/clang++ "$@"\n' > /opt/sccache-wrappers/clang++ \
+        && chmod +x /opt/sccache-wrappers/clang++ \
+        && printf '#!/bin/bash\nexec sccache /opt/rocm/lib/llvm/bin/clang "$@"\n' > /opt/sccache-wrappers/clang \
+        && chmod +x /opt/sccache-wrappers/clang \
+        && echo "sccache wrappers created in /opt/sccache-wrappers"; \
+    fi
+
+# Set sccache environment variables only when USE_SCCACHE=1
+# This prevents S3 config from leaking into images when sccache is not used
+ARG USE_SCCACHE
+ENV SCCACHE_BUCKET=${USE_SCCACHE:+${SCCACHE_BUCKET_NAME}}
+ENV SCCACHE_REGION=${USE_SCCACHE:+${SCCACHE_REGION_NAME}}
+ENV SCCACHE_S3_NO_CREDENTIALS=${USE_SCCACHE:+${SCCACHE_S3_NO_CREDENTIALS}}
+ENV SCCACHE_IDLE_TIMEOUT=${USE_SCCACHE:+0}
+
+
+###
+### Triton Build
+###
+FROM base AS build_triton
+ARG TRITON_BRANCH
+ARG TRITON_REPO
+RUN git clone ${TRITON_REPO}
+RUN cd triton \
+    && git checkout ${TRITON_BRANCH} \
+    && git config --global user.email "you@example.com" && git config --global user.name "Your Name" \
+    && if [ ! -f setup.py ]; then cd python; fi \
+    && MAX_JOBS=16 python3 setup.py bdist_wheel --dist-dir=dist \
+    && mkdir -p /app/install && cp dist/*.whl /app/install
+
+
+###
+### AMD SMI Build
+###
+FROM base AS build_amdsmi
+RUN cd /opt/rocm/share/amd_smi \
+    && pip wheel . --wheel-dir=dist
+RUN mkdir -p /app/install && cp /opt/rocm/share/amd_smi/dist/*.whl /app/install
+
+
+###
+### Pytorch build
+###
+FROM base AS build_pytorch
+ARG PYTORCH_BRANCH
+ARG PYTORCH_REPO
+ARG USE_SCCACHE
+
+RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y pkg-config liblzma-dev
+# torch 2.12 emits float->__bf16 libcalls (__truncsfbf2) absent from gcc-11 libgcc; build with gcc-13.
+RUN update-alternatives --install /usr/bin/gcc gcc /usr/bin/gcc-13 130 --slave /usr/bin/g++ g++ /usr/bin/g++-13
+RUN git clone ${PYTORCH_REPO} pytorch
+RUN cd pytorch && git checkout ${PYTORCH_BRANCH}
+RUN cd pytorch \
+    && pip install -r requirements.txt && git submodule update --init --recursive
+RUN cd pytorch && python3 tools/amd_build/build_amd.py \
+    && if [ "$USE_SCCACHE" = "1" ]; then \
+           export HIP_CLANG_PATH=/opt/sccache-wrappers \
+           && export CMAKE_C_COMPILER_LAUNCHER=sccache \
+           && export CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER_LAUNCHER=sccache \
+           && sccache --show-stats; \
+       fi \
+    && CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH=$(python3 -c 'import sys; print(sys.prefix)') python3 setup.py bdist_wheel --dist-dir=dist \
+    && if [ "$USE_SCCACHE" = "1" ]; then sccache --show-stats; fi
+RUN mkdir -p /app/install && cp /app/pytorch/dist/*.whl /app/install
+
+
+###
+### Shared PyTorch runtime for dependent builds
+###
+FROM base AS build_pytorch_runtime
+RUN update-alternatives --install /usr/bin/gcc gcc /usr/bin/gcc-13 130 --slave /usr/bin/g++ g++ /usr/bin/g++-13
+RUN --mount=type=bind,from=build_pytorch,src=/app/install/,target=/install,ro \
+    pip install /install/*.whl
+
+
+###
+### TorchVision build
+###
+FROM build_pytorch_runtime AS build_torchvision
+ARG PYTORCH_VISION_BRANCH
+ARG PYTORCH_VISION_REPO
+ARG USE_SCCACHE
+
+RUN git clone ${PYTORCH_VISION_REPO} vision
+RUN cd vision && git checkout ${PYTORCH_VISION_BRANCH} \
+    && if [ "$USE_SCCACHE" = "1" ]; then \
+           export HIP_CLANG_PATH=/opt/sccache-wrappers \
+           && export CMAKE_C_COMPILER_LAUNCHER=sccache \
+           && export CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER_LAUNCHER=sccache; \
+       fi \
+    && python3 setup.py bdist_wheel --dist-dir=dist \
+    && if [ "$USE_SCCACHE" = "1" ]; then sccache --show-stats; fi
+RUN mkdir -p /app/install && cp /app/vision/dist/*.whl /app/install
+
+
+###
+### TorchAudio build
+###
+FROM build_pytorch_runtime AS build_torchaudio
+ARG PYTORCH_AUDIO_BRANCH
+ARG PYTORCH_AUDIO_REPO
+ARG USE_SCCACHE
+
+RUN git clone ${PYTORCH_AUDIO_REPO} audio
+RUN cd audio && git checkout ${PYTORCH_AUDIO_BRANCH} \
+    && git submodule update --init --recursive
+RUN cd audio && pip install -r requirements.txt
+RUN cd audio \
+    && if [ "$USE_SCCACHE" = "1" ]; then \
+           export HIP_CLANG_PATH=/opt/sccache-wrappers \
+           && export CMAKE_C_COMPILER_LAUNCHER=sccache \
+           && export CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER_LAUNCHER=sccache; \
+       fi \
+    && python3 setup.py bdist_wheel --dist-dir=dist \
+    && if [ "$USE_SCCACHE" = "1" ]; then sccache --show-stats; fi
+RUN mkdir -p /app/install && cp /app/audio/dist/*.whl /app/install
+
+
+###
+### MORI Build
+###
+FROM base AS build_mori
+ARG MORI_BRANCH
+ARG MORI_REPO
+RUN --mount=type=bind,from=build_pytorch,src=/app/install/,target=/install \
+    pip install /install/*.whl
+RUN git clone ${MORI_REPO}
+RUN cd mori \
+    && git checkout ${MORI_BRANCH} \
+    && git submodule update --init --recursive \
+    && python3 setup.py bdist_wheel --dist-dir=dist && ls /app/mori/dist/*.whl
+RUN mkdir -p /app/install && cp /app/mori/dist/*.whl /app/install
+
+
+###
+### FlashAttention Build
+###
+FROM base AS build_fa
+ARG FA_BRANCH
+ARG FA_REPO
+ARG USE_SCCACHE
+RUN --mount=type=bind,from=build_pytorch,src=/app/install/,target=/install \
+    pip install /install/*.whl
+RUN git clone ${FA_REPO}
+RUN cd flash-attention \
+    && git checkout ${FA_BRANCH} \
+    && git submodule update --init \
+    && if [ "$USE_SCCACHE" = "1" ]; then \
+           export HIP_CLANG_PATH=/opt/sccache-wrappers \
+           && sccache --show-stats; \
+       fi \
+    && GPU_ARCHS=$(echo ${PYTORCH_ROCM_ARCH} | sed -e 's/;gfx1[0-9]\{3\}//g') python3 setup.py bdist_wheel --dist-dir=dist \
+    && if [ "$USE_SCCACHE" = "1" ]; then sccache --show-stats; fi
+RUN mkdir -p /app/install && cp /app/flash-attention/dist/*.whl /app/install
+
+
+###
+### AITER Build
+###
+FROM base AS build_aiter
+ARG AITER_BRANCH
+ARG AITER_REPO
+ARG USE_SCCACHE
+RUN --mount=type=bind,from=build_pytorch,src=/app/install/,target=/install \
+    pip install /install/*.whl
+RUN git clone --recursive --branch ${AITER_BRANCH} ${AITER_REPO}
+RUN cd aiter \
+    && git submodule update --init --recursive \
+    && pip install -r requirements.txt
+RUN pip install pyyaml && cd aiter \
+    && if [ "$USE_SCCACHE" = "1" ]; then \
+           export HIP_CLANG_PATH=/opt/sccache-wrappers \
+           && sccache --show-stats; \
+       fi \
+    && PREBUILD_KERNELS=1 AITER_USE_SYSTEM_TRITON=1 GPU_ARCHS=${AITER_ROCM_ARCH} python3 setup.py bdist_wheel --dist-dir=dist \
+    && if [ "$USE_SCCACHE" = "1" ]; then sccache --show-stats; fi \
+    && ls /app/aiter/dist/*.whl
+RUN mkdir -p /app/install && cp /app/aiter/dist/*.whl /app/install
+
+
+###
+### Final Build
+###
+
+# Wheel release stage - 
+# only includes dependencies used by wheel release pipeline
+FROM base AS debs_wheel_release
+RUN mkdir /app/debs
+RUN --mount=type=bind,from=build_triton,src=/app/install/,target=/install \
+    cp /install/*.whl /app/debs
+RUN --mount=type=bind,from=build_fa,src=/app/install/,target=/install \
+    cp /install/*.whl /app/debs
+RUN --mount=type=bind,from=build_amdsmi,src=/app/install/,target=/install \
+    cp /install/*.whl /app/debs
+RUN --mount=type=bind,from=build_pytorch,src=/app/install/,target=/install \
+    cp /install/*.whl /app/debs
+RUN --mount=type=bind,from=build_torchvision,src=/app/install/,target=/install \
+    cp /install/*.whl /app/debs
+RUN --mount=type=bind,from=build_torchaudio,src=/app/install/,target=/install \
+    cp /install/*.whl /app/debs
+RUN --mount=type=bind,from=build_aiter,src=/app/install/,target=/install \
+    cp /install/*.whl /app/debs
+
+# Full debs stage - includes Mori (used by Docker releases)
+FROM base AS debs
+RUN mkdir /app/debs
+RUN --mount=type=bind,from=build_triton,src=/app/install/,target=/install \
+    cp /install/*.whl /app/debs
+RUN --mount=type=bind,from=build_fa,src=/app/install/,target=/install \
+    cp /install/*.whl /app/debs
+RUN --mount=type=bind,from=build_amdsmi,src=/app/install/,target=/install \
+    cp /install/*.whl /app/debs
+RUN --mount=type=bind,from=build_pytorch,src=/app/install/,target=/install \
+    cp /install/*.whl /app/debs
+RUN --mount=type=bind,from=build_torchvision,src=/app/install/,target=/install \
+    cp /install/*.whl /app/debs
+RUN --mount=type=bind,from=build_torchaudio,src=/app/install/,target=/install \
+    cp /install/*.whl /app/debs
+RUN --mount=type=bind,from=build_aiter,src=/app/install/,target=/install \
+    cp /install/*.whl /app/debs
+RUN --mount=type=bind,from=build_mori,src=/app/install/,target=/install \
+    cp /install/*.whl /app/debs
+
+###
+### ROCr + CLR build
+###
+# Pull in updates to ROCr + clr from ROCm 7.2.4 and beyond.
+FROM base AS build_rocm_runtime
+ARG ROCM_SYSTEMS_REPO
+ARG ROCM_RUNTIME_COMMIT
+RUN apt-get update \
+    && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends g++ \
+       libelf-dev libdrm-dev libnuma-dev libdw-dev xxd \
+    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
+RUN pip install --no-cache-dir CppHeaderParser
+RUN git init -q /src && cd /src \
+    && git remote add origin ${ROCM_SYSTEMS_REPO} \
+    && git config core.sparseCheckout true \
+    && git config remote.origin.promisor true \
+    && git config remote.origin.partialclonefilter blob:none \
+    && git sparse-checkout init --cone \
+    && git sparse-checkout set projects/rocr-runtime projects/clr projects/hip shared cmake \
+    && git fetch --filter=blob:none --depth 1 origin ${ROCM_RUNTIME_COMMIT} \
+    && git checkout -q FETCH_HEAD
+# ROCr's trap_handler and blit_shaders call find_package(Clang/LLVM REQUIRED) only to get
+# IMPORTED executables. The ROCm dev image ships the binaries but no CMake package config, so
+# supply one pointing at them.

+### Threading model
+
+Tier methods run in the scheduler process, under the tiering manager's lock, so they are never entered concurrently. They are not always called from the same thread, though.
+
+Most tiers only ever see the scheduler thread, which holds the lock for the length of one engine step. A tier whose counterpart is not driven by the engine — the `p2p` tier, answering a remote peer — needs servicing while the engine is busy running the model, because otherwise a peer's lookup or fetch waits for the next step boundary. On a saturated rank that wait can be seconds, dwarfing the transfer it gates. Such tiers set `tolerates_off_thread_polling`, and the tiering manager runs one tier-poll thread that, once per `tier_poll_interval_s`, polls them for finished jobs and lets them serve external requests. A tier that implements `serve_external_requests()` without setting the flag is served once per engine step only.
+
+Two consequences worth knowing:
+
+- Any tier can be reached from that thread indirectly, because serving a peer looks keys up through the tiering manager, which fans out to the other tiers. Tier state must therefore not assume a particular thread, only that the manager lock is held.
+- Work the thread deliberately leaves alone is batched per step: a promotion it initiates is submitted at the next `on_schedule_end()`, not immediately.
+
+Setting `tier_poll_interval_s` to `0` disables the thread; opted-in tiers then get serviced once per engine step, as they were before it existed.

+## Explicit pool sizing for `SimpleCPUOffloadConnector`
+
+`SimpleCPUOffloadConnector` accepts an optional `num_cpu_blocks` in
+`kv_connector_extra_config`. The scheduler and every worker use this exact
+number of offload blocks instead of automatic sizing from
+`cpu_bytes_to_use_per_rank` or `cpu_bytes_to_use / world_size`.
+Use the same positive integer on all ranks, chosen
+to fit the smallest per-worker capacity. This supports pipeline stages with
+different KV cache sizes without adding a collective during initialization.
+
+```json
+{
+  "kv_connector": "SimpleCPUOffloadConnector",
+  "kv_role": "kv_both",
+  "kv_connector_extra_config": {
+    "cpu_bytes_to_use_per_rank": 1073741824,
+    "num_cpu_blocks": 64,
+    "lazy_offload": false
+  }
+}
+```
+
+The example count must be adjusted for the model, KV layout, and parallelism.
+The configured byte budget remains an upper bound: startup fails if the
+requested count exceeds a worker's capacity. For the `disk` backend the count
+selects disk slots and is checked against `disk_capacity_bytes`. Omitting
+`num_cpu_blocks` preserves automatic per-worker sizing. This option applies
+to `SimpleCPUOffloadConnector`, separately from `OffloadingConnector` above.

+# Routed Experts Return (MoE Routing Replay / R3)
+
+`--enable-return-routed-experts` makes vLLM return the routed experts (the expert IDs each MoE layer's router selected) for every token of a request. RL trainers use it for MoE routing replay (R3): the training forward pass reuses the rollout's routing.
+
+```bash
+vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B --enable-return-routed-experts
+# offline: LLM("Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B", enable_return_routed_experts=True)
+```
+
+The flag sets `AuxOutputConfig.enable_return_routed_experts` (full form: `--aux-output-config '{"enable_return_routed_experts": true, "max_bytes": N}'`). There is no per-request on/off switch.
+
+## Requirements
+
+Startup fails with a `ValueError` unless:
+
+- **Model Runner V2** is used (`VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1` if vLLM falls back to V1);
+- the runner is `generate` and the model is **MoE**;
+- **prefix caching is enabled** (the default). `--no-enable-prefix-caching` fails; the old v0.21 advice to disable it is wrong.
+
+Rejected at startup: adaptive speculative verification, PP > 1, DCP/PCP > 1, and the `NixlConnector`, `NixlPullConnector`, `NixlPushConnector`, `MoRIIOConnector`, `MooncakeConnector` KV connectors. Regular speculative decoding works.
+
+### How it works: aux output connector
+
+Routing is stored by the aux output connector (`vllm/distributed/aux_output_connector/`, configured via `--aux-output-config`), keyed by KV block hash and shared with prefix caching, which is why prefix caching is required. `max_bytes` is its host-memory LRU capacity (default: derived from KV cache capacity). If a prefix-cache hit needs evicted rows, the worker raises `BlockObjectStoreError`; increase `max_bytes`.
+
+## Output format
+
+| API | Field |
+| --- | --- |
+| Offline (`LLM`, `AsyncLLM`) | `CompletionOutput.routed_experts`: `np.ndarray` or `None` |
+| `/v1/completions`, `/v1/chat/completions` | `choices[i].routed_experts`: base64 `.npy`, **non-streaming only** |
+| `/inference/v1/generate` | `routed_experts` per choice (base64 `.npy`); with `stream: true`, on the final chunk |
+
+- **Shape:** `(num_tokens - 1 - routed_experts_prompt_start, num_moe_layers, num_experts_per_tok)`, `num_tokens` = prompt + output. The last sampled token has no row.
+- **Rows:** row `i` is position `routed_experts_prompt_start + i` of `prompt_token_ids + output_token_ids`.
+- **dtype:** `uint8` for at most 256 experts, else `uint16`; logical expert IDs.
+- Filled only when the request finishes. `None` if the flag is off or the request aborted before any forward pass.
+
+```python
+import base64, io
+import numpy as np
+
+experts = np.load(io.BytesIO(base64.b64decode(choice["routed_experts"])))
+```
+
+## `routed_experts_prompt_start`
+
+Per-request, default `0`: drops the first N prompt-token rows (e.g. routing already received in earlier turns). Must be `0 <= value <= prompt_len`, else HTTP 400. Pass it top-level on `/v1/*completions`, inside `sampling_params` on `/inference/v1/generate`, or as `SamplingParams(routed_experts_prompt_start=...)`.
+
+## Limitations
+
+- The Rust HTTP frontend never returns `routed_experts` and always sends `routed_experts_prompt_start = 0`. Use the Python API server.
+
+Example: [examples/rl/routed_experts_e2e.py](../../examples/rl/routed_experts_e2e.py).

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""CUDA IPC weight sync over HTTP from a trainer that never imports vLLM.
+
+The trainer uses only `torch`, `requests`, `safetensors`, `pybase64` and the
+stdlib, and speaks the wire protocol in
+`docs/training/weight_transfer/ipc.md` ("Trainer Without vLLM over HTTP"):
+it exports its tensors with `torch.multiprocessing.reductions.reduce_tensor`
+and sends the handles, pickled and base64-encoded, in `ipc_handles_pickled`.
+
+IPC requires colocation: this process holds a full copy of the weights on every
+GPU the server uses, and keys each handle by that GPU's UUID. A multi-process
+trainer would instead gather the per-rank `{uuid: args}` dicts to one rank.
+
+Start a server; IPC handles are pickled, so it needs
+`VLLM_ALLOW_INSECURE_SERIALIZATION=1` (the weights it starts with are discarded):
+
+    VLLM_SERVER_DEV_MODE=1 VLLM_ALLOW_INSECURE_SERIALIZATION=1 \
+        CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B \
+        --load-format dummy --enforce-eager --gpu-memory-utilization 0.4 \
+        --weight-transfer-config '{"backend": "ipc"}'
+
+Then run the trainer on the same GPU(s) (`--packed` for chunked transfer):
+
+    CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 python examples/rl/rlhf_http_ipc_no_vllm.py \
+        --checkpoint /path/to/Qwen3-0.6B
+
+For a TP=2 server on GPUs 0-1, use `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1` on both sides and
+pass `--num-gpus 2` to the trainer.
+"""
+
+import sys
+
+
+class _BlockVLLM:
+    def find_spec(self, name, path=None, target=None):
+        if name.split(".")[0] == "vllm":
+            raise ImportError(f"this trainer must not import {name!r}")
+        return None
+
+
+sys.meta_path.insert(0, _BlockVLLM())
+
+import argparse  # noqa: E402
+import glob  # noqa: E402
+import pickle  # noqa: E402
+
+import pybase64 as base64  # noqa: E402
+import requests  # noqa: E402
+import torch  # noqa: E402
+from safetensors.torch import load_file  # noqa: E402
+from torch.multiprocessing.reductions import reduce_tensor  # noqa: E402
+
+parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
+parser.add_argument("--url", default="http://localhost:8000")
+parser.add_argument("--checkpoint", required=True, help="dir with *.safetensors")
+parser.add_argument("--num-gpus", type=int, default=1)
+parser.add_argument("--packed", action="store_true")
+parser.add_argument("--packed-buffer-size-bytes", type=int, default=512 << 20)
+args = parser.parse_args()
+
+
+def post(path: str, body: dict | None = None) -> dict:
+    r = requests.post(args.url + path, json=body or {}, timeout=600)
+    r.raise_for_status()
+    return r.json()
+
+
+def generate(prompts: list[str]) -> list[str]:
+    model = requests.get(args.url + "/v1/models", timeout=60).json()["data"][0]["id"]
+    body = {"model": model, "prompt": prompts, "max_tokens": 16, "temperature": 0}
+    choices = post("/v1/completions", body)["choices"]
+    return [c["text"] for c in sorted(choices, key=lambda c: c["index"])]
+
+
+# Weights are {gpu_uuid: {name: tensor}}: one full copy per colocated GPU. The
+# UUID is str(torch.cuda.get_device_properties(i).uuid), with no "GPU-" prefix.
+Weights = dict[str, dict[str, torch.Tensor]]
+
+
+def update_weights(
+    weights: Weights,
+    names: list[str],
+    ipc_handles: list[dict[str, tuple]] | dict[str, tuple],
+    tensor_sizes: list[int] | None = None,
+) -> None:
+    w = next(iter(weights.values()))
+    update_info = {
+        "names": names,
+        "dtype_names": [str(w[n].dtype).removeprefix("torch.") for n in names],
+        "shapes": [list(w[n].shape) for n in names],
+        "ipc_handles_pickled": base64.b64encode(pickle.dumps(ipc_handles)).decode(),
+    }
+    if tensor_sizes is not None:
+        update_info["tensor_sizes"] = tensor_sizes
+    post("/update_weights", {"update_info": update_info})
+
+
+def send_unpacked(weights: Weights, names: list[str]) -> list[torch.Tensor]:
+    """One /update_weights call; one {uuid: args} dict per parameter."""
+    copies = {u: {n: w[n].contiguous() for n in names} for u, w in weights.items()}
+    handles = [{u: reduce_tensor(copies[u][n])[1] for u in copies} for n in names]
+    update_weights(weights, names, handles)
+    return [t for c in copies.values() for t in c.values()]
+
+
+def send_packed(weights: Weights, names: list[str], cap: int) -> list[torch.Tensor]:
+    """One /update_weights call per chunk; one {uuid: args} dict per chunk."""
+    buffers = {
+        u: torch.empty(cap, dtype=torch.uint8, device=w[names[0]].device)
+        for u, w in weights.items()
+    }
+    handle = {u: reduce_tensor(b)[1] for u, b in buffers.items()}  # export once
+    chunk: list[str] = []
+    sizes: list[int] = []
+
+    def flush() -> None:
+        for b in buffers.values():
+            torch.accelerator.synchronize(b.device)  # copies must land before the read
+        update_weights(weights, chunk, handle, sizes)
+        chunk.clear()
+        sizes.clear()

+    for n in names:

+            flush()

+            flat = w[n].contiguous().view(-1).view(torch.uint8)
+            buffers[u][offset : offset + nbytes].copy_(flat)
+        chunk.append(n)
+        sizes.append(nbytes)
+    if chunk:
+        flush()
+    return list(buffers.values())
+
+

+    weights: Weights = {}
+    for i in range(args.num_gpus):
+        uuid = str(torch.cuda.get_device_properties(i).uuid)
+        weights[uuid] = {}

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""NCCL weight sync over HTTP from a trainer that never imports vLLM.
+
+The trainer uses only `torch`, `requests`, `safetensors`, `pybase64` and the
+stdlib, and speaks the wire protocol in
+`docs/training/weight_transfer/nccl.md` ("Trainer Without vLLM over HTTP"):
+`nccl_unique_id_b64` rendezvous, a one-element warm-up `all_reduce`, then
+`/start_weight_update` -> `/update_weights` (concurrent with the rank-0
+broadcast) -> `/finish_weight_update`.
+
+The NCCL communicator is a plain `torch.distributed.ProcessGroupNCCL` over a
+private `TCPStore` that only the trainer joins. Its `ncclUniqueId` is read back
+from store key "0", which is a torch implementation detail.
+
+Start a server on GPUs 0-1 (the weights it starts with are discarded):
+
+    VLLM_SERVER_DEV_MODE=1 CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1 vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B \
+        --tensor-parallel-size 2 --load-format dummy --enforce-eager \
+        --weight-transfer-config '{"backend": "nccl"}'
+
+Then run the trainer on GPU 2 (`--packed` for packed broadcasting):
+
+    CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=2 python examples/rl/rlhf_http_nccl_no_vllm.py \
+        --checkpoint /path/to/Qwen3-0.6B
+"""
+
+import sys
+
+
+class _BlockVLLM:
+    def find_spec(self, name, path=None, target=None):
+        if name.split(".")[0] == "vllm":
+            raise ImportError(f"this trainer must not import {name!r}")
+        return None
+
+
+sys.meta_path.insert(0, _BlockVLLM())
+
+import argparse  # noqa: E402
+import datetime  # noqa: E402
+import glob  # noqa: E402
+import threading  # noqa: E402
+
+import pybase64 as base64  # noqa: E402
+import requests  # noqa: E402
+import torch  # noqa: E402
+import torch.distributed as dist  # noqa: E402
+from safetensors.torch import load_file  # noqa: E402
+
+parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
+parser.add_argument("--url", default="http://localhost:8000")
+parser.add_argument("--checkpoint", required=True, help="dir with *.safetensors")
+parser.add_argument("--packed", action="store_true")
+parser.add_argument("--packed-buffer-size-bytes", type=int, default=64 << 20)
+parser.add_argument("--store-port", type=int, default=29612)
+args = parser.parse_args()
+
+
+def post(path: str, body: dict | None = None) -> dict:
+    r = requests.post(args.url + path, json=body or {}, timeout=600)
+    r.raise_for_status()
+    return r.json()
+
+
+class PostInBackground(threading.Thread):
+    """An HTTP call that only returns once this process joins the collective."""
+
+    def __init__(self, path: str, body: dict) -> None:
+        super().__init__()
+        self.path, self.body = path, body
+        self.error: BaseException | None = None
+        self.start()
+
+    def run(self) -> None:
+        try:
+            post(self.path, self.body)
+        except BaseException as e:
+            self.error = e
+
+    def result(self) -> None:
+        self.join()
+        if self.error is not None:
+            raise self.error
+
+
+def generate(prompts: list[str]) -> list[str]:
+    model = requests.get(args.url + "/v1/models", timeout=60).json()["data"][0]["id"]
+    body = {"model": model, "prompt": prompts, "max_tokens": 16, "temperature": 0}
+    choices = post("/v1/completions", body)["choices"]
+    return [c["text"] for c in sorted(choices, key=lambda c: c["index"])]
+
+
+def main() -> None:
+    device = torch.device("cuda:0")
+    torch.accelerator.set_device_index(device)
+    weights: dict[str, torch.Tensor] = {}
+    for path in sorted(glob.glob(f"{args.checkpoint}/*.safetensors")):
+        weights.update(load_file(path, device="cuda:0"))
+    names = sorted(weights)
+
+    prompts = ["The capital of France is", "def fibonacci(n):"]
+    print("before:", generate(prompts))
+
+    # Trainer is NCCL rank 0; vLLM worker i is rank 1 + i.
+    world_size = 1 + requests.get(args.url + "/get_world_size").json()["world_size"]
+    store = dist.TCPStore(
+        "127.0.0.1", args.store_port, is_master=True, wait_for_workers=False
+    )
+    pg = dist.ProcessGroupNCCL(store, 0, world_size, dist.ProcessGroupNCCL.Options())
+    connect = threading.Thread(target=pg.eager_connect_single_device, args=(device,))
+    connect.start()  # publishes the unique id, then waits in ncclCommInitRank
+    reader = dist.TCPStore("127.0.0.1", args.store_port, is_master=False)
+    reader.wait(["0"], datetime.timedelta(seconds=60))
+    unique_id = reader.get("0")
+    assert len(unique_id) == 128
+
+    init = PostInBackground(
+        "/init_weight_transfer_engine",
+        {
+            "init_info": {
+                "nccl_unique_id_b64": base64.b64encode(unique_id).decode(),
+                "rank_offset": 1,
+                "world_size": world_size,
+                "packed": args.packed,
+                "packed_buffer_size_bytes": args.packed_buffer_size_bytes,
+            }
+        },
+    )
+    connect.join()
+    pg.allreduce([torch.zeros(1, device=device)]).wait()  # vLLM's warm-up
+    init.result()
+
+    def broadcast(t: torch.Tensor) -> None:
+        opts = dist.BroadcastOptions()
+        opts.rootRank = 0
+        pg.broadcast([t], opts).wait()
+
+    post("/start_weight_update")
+    update_info = {
+        "names": names,
+        "dtype_names": [str(weights[n].dtype).removeprefix("torch.") for n in names],
+        "shapes": [list(weights[n].shape) for n in names],
+    }
+    update = PostInBackground("/update_weights", {"update_info": update_info})
+    if not args.packed:
+        for n in names:
+            broadcast(weights[n].contiguous())
+    else:
+        # Same chunking as the worker: a chunk closes right after the tensor
+        # that pushes it past the buffer size.
+        chunk: list[torch.Tensor] = []
+        size = 0
+        for n in names:
+            chunk.append(weights[n].contiguous().view(-1).view(torch.uint8))
+            size += chunk[-1].numel()
+            if size > args.packed_buffer_size_bytes:
+                broadcast(torch.cat(chunk))
+                chunk, size = [], 0
+        if chunk:
+            broadcast(torch.cat(chunk))
+    torch.accelerator.synchronize()
+    update.result()
+    post("/finish_weight_update", {"weight_version": None})
+
+    print("after: ", generate(prompts))
+    post("/shutdown_weight_transfer_engine")
+    pg.shutdown()
+
+    assert not [m for m in sys.modules if m.split(".")[0] == "vllm"]
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()

+# vLLM model recipes
+
+This directory holds the deployment recipes for models served by vLLM, one
+YAML per model at `models/<hf_org>/<hf_repo>.yaml`. The path mirrors the
+Hugging Face ID, so `models/Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B.yaml` renders at
+[recipes.vllm.ai/Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B](https://recipes.vllm.ai/Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B).
+
+The site, the command builder, and the JSON API are built by
+[vllm-project/recipes](https://github.com/vllm-project/recipes). That
+repository owns the schema and the shared vocabulary (hardware profiles,
+serving strategies, KV-offload deployments) and pins this directory to a
+commit. Omni (image, video, audio) recipes stay in vllm-project/recipes for
+now (moving to vllm-omni), and Ascend NPU content is inline in these recipes
+(moving to vllm-ascend overlays).
+
+## Editing a recipe
+
+Start a new recipe from
+[`templates/recipe.yaml`](https://github.com/vllm-project/recipes/blob/main/templates/recipe.yaml).
+Fields are defined in
+[SCHEMA.md](https://github.com/vllm-project/recipes/blob/main/SCHEMA.md) and
+checked against [`recipe.schema.json`](https://recipes.vllm.ai/recipe.schema.json)
+on every build; an unknown or misspelled key is an error. For completion and
+inline errors in YAML-aware editors, start the file with
+`# yaml-language-server: $schema=https://recipes.vllm.ai/recipe.schema.json`.
+
+Follow the recipes repository's
+[add-recipe skill](https://github.com/vllm-project/recipes/blob/main/.agents/skills/add-recipe/SKILL.md)
+for the schema and the validation steps. To validate a change exactly as this
+repository's `Recipes` PR check does, run from a checkout of
+`vllm-project/recipes`:
+
+```bash
+node scripts/validate-source.mjs --source vllm --dir ~/vllm/recipes
+```
+
+To preview the site with your changes, add a gitignored `sources.local.yaml`
+to that checkout with `overrides: { vllm: ~/vllm/recipes }` and run `pnpm dev`.
+This works once vllm-project/recipes reads this directory as its `vllm`
+source (vllm-project/recipes#1095).

+guide: |
+  ## Overview
+
+  [DiffusionGemma 26B-A4B](https://huggingface.co/google/diffusiongemma-26B-A4B-it) is a block-diffusion language model built on Gemma 4's MoE backbone. Instead of generating tokens one at a time (autoregressive), it generates blocks of 256 tokens simultaneously via iterative denoising over a fixed canvas — trading higher time-to-first-token for significantly higher per-request generation throughput.
+
+  ### Key Architecture Features
+  - **Block Diffusion**: Generates tokens in 256-token canvas blocks via iterative denoising (up to 48 steps per block).
+  - **MoE Backbone**: Same Gemma 4 architecture — 128 fine-grained experts with top-8 routing, 26B total / 4B active parameters.
+  - **Entropy-Bound Sampling**: Uses an entropy-based sampler (`diffusion_sampler: entropy_bound`, `entropy_bound: 0.1`) for the denoising process.
+  - **Multimodal**: Supports text + images via the Gemma 4 vision encoder.
+  - **Thinking Mode**: Supports structured reasoning via `<|channel>thought\n...<channel|>` delimiters.
+  - **Function Calling**: Supports Gemma 4's tool-call protocol (works best in thinking mode).
+
+  ### Important Deployment Notes
+
+  DiffusionGemma requires several specific flags that differ from standard Gemma 4:
+
+  | Flag | Why |
+  |------|-----|
+  | `--max-num-seqs 4` | The diffusion state buffers (`self_conditioning_probs`) pre-allocate `max_seqs × canvas_length × vocab_size` tensors. With Gemma's 262K vocab and canvas_length=256, higher values cause OOM. |
+  | `--generation-config vllm` | The checkpoint's `generation_config.json` sets `max_tokens: 256`, which would override per-request limits. This flag ignores it. |
+  | `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.85` | Leaves headroom for activation memory during denoising. |
+  | `--hf-overrides '{"diffusion_sampler":"entropy_bound","diffusion_entropy_bound":0.1}'` | Configures the entropy-bound denoising sampler. |
+  | `--diffusion-config '{"canvas_length": 256}'` | Sets the canvas block size for generation. |
+
+  ## Prerequisites
+
+  DiffusionGemma requires a vLLM build with diffusion model support, available in the
+  Gemma docker image:
+
+  ```bash
+  docker pull vllm/vllm-openai:gemma
+  ```
+
+  ## Deployment
+
+  ### Single GPU (H100/H200, BF16)
+
+  ```bash
+  docker run -itd --name diffusiongemma \
+      --ipc=host --network host --gpus all \
+      -v ~/.cache/huggingface:/root/.cache/huggingface \
+      vllm/vllm-openai:gemma \
+          --model google/diffusiongemma-26B-A4B-it \
+          --max-model-len 262144 \
+          --max-num-seqs 4 \
+          --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 \
+          --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000
+  ```
+
+  ### Intel Xeon 6 (CPU, BF16)
+
+  DiffusionGemma runs on Intel Xeon 6 CPUs using vLLM's CPU backend with AMX BF16 acceleration.
+  The generated example uses TP=1. Adjust `--tensor-parallel-size` based on the
+  detected NUMA topology and deployment requirements.
+
+  ```bash
+  docker run \
+    --privileged --ipc=host -p 8000:8000 \
+    -v ~/.cache/huggingface:/root/.cache/huggingface \
+    vllm/vllm-openai-cpu:latest-x86_64 google/diffusiongemma-26B-A4B-it \
+    --max-num-seqs 4 \
+    --tensor-parallel-size 1 \
+    --enable-auto-tool-choice \
+    --tool-call-parser gemma4 \
+    --chat-template examples/tool_chat_template_gemma4.jinja \
+    --reasoning-parser gemma4
+  ```
+
+
+  ### Intel XPU (B60 / B70, BF16)
+
+  Validated on 4x Intel Arc Pro B60 / B70 (B60 24 GB, B70 32 GB per card)
+  with the official vLLM XPU image `vllm/vllm-openai-xpu:latest`. `--enforce-eager`
+  and `--attention-backend TRITON_ATTN` are required on this backend. Select Arc Pro
+  B60/B70 in the hardware picker above for the exact command.
+
+  ### Full-Featured Server (text + image + thinking + tools)
+
+  ```bash
+  docker run -itd --name diffusiongemma \
+      --ipc=host --network host --gpus all \
+      -v ~/.cache/huggingface:/root/.cache/huggingface \
+      vllm/vllm-openai:gemma \
+          --model google/diffusiongemma-26B-A4B-it \
+          --max-model-len 262144 \
+          --max-num-seqs 4 \
+          --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 \
+          --mm-processor-kwargs '{"max_soft_tokens": 1120}' \
+          --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image": 7}' \
+          --enable-auto-tool-choice \
+          --tool-call-parser gemma4 \
+          --reasoning-parser gemma4 \
+          --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000
+  ```
+
+  ### Jev-Style Structured Decisions (Nightly)
+
+  vLLM's structured-read support for DiffusionGemma can answer yes/no, multiple-choice,
+  and scored questions with a confidence value. The example server seeds a canvas with
+  the response template, leaves only the answer slots noisy, and reads a probability
+  distribution from every slot after one denoising step. It exposes the Jev-compatible
+  `/v1/systemone` endpoint; this is an example server rather than a standard vLLM endpoint.
+
+  Use the pinned nightly image that contains the merged structured-read support:
+
+  ```bash
+  docker run -d --name dgemma \
+      --gpus '"device=0"' \
+      --ipc=host \
+      -p 8000:8000 \
+      -p 8011:8011 \
+      -v "$HOME/.cache/huggingface:/root/.cache/huggingface" \
+      vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-e9757321527ca1ecd514c07c1418dd2c53da3d19 \
+      google/diffusiongemma-26B-A4B-it \
+      --served-model-name dgemma \
+      --diffusion-config '{"canvas_length":64}' \
+      --max-logprobs 32 \
+      --enable-prefix-caching
+  ```
+
+  Wait for the vLLM server to become healthy, then start the example server in the same
+  container:
+
+  ```bash
+  until curl -fsS localhost:8000/health >/dev/null; do sleep 2; done
+
+  docker exec -d dgemma \
+      python /vllm-workspace/examples/features/structured_diffusion/structured_server.py \
+      --upstream http://127.0.0.1:8000 \
+      --tokenizer google/diffusiongemma-26B-A4B-it \
+      --canvas 64
+  ```
+
+  After the example server becomes healthy, send a Jev-style decision request:
+
+  ```bash
+  until curl -fsS localhost:8011/health >/dev/null; do sleep 2; done
+
+  curl -sS localhost:8011/v1/systemone \
+      -H 'content-type: application/json' \
+      -d '{
+        "model": "jev-latest",
+        "state": {"ticket": "Everything is down, demo at noon."},
+        "questions": {
+          "urgent": {
+            "type": "noul",
+            "instructions": "Needs a reply within the hour?"
+          }
+        }
+      }'
+  ```
+
+  ## Client Usage
+
+  ### Text Generation
+
+  ```python
+  from openai import OpenAI
+
+  client = OpenAI(base_url="http://localhost:8000/v1", api_key="EMPTY")
+  response = client.chat.completions.create(
+      model="google/diffusiongemma-26B-A4B-it",
+      messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Write a poem about the ocean."}],
+      max_tokens=512,
+      temperature=0.7,
+  )
+  print(response.choices[0].message.content)
+  ```
+
+  ### Offline Inference
+
+  ```python
+  from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams
+  from transformers import AutoTokenizer
+
+  model_path = "google/diffusiongemma-26B-A4B-it"
+  tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_path)
+
+  llm = LLM(
+      model=model_path,
+      max_num_seqs=4,
+      gpu_memory_utilization=0.85,
+      hf_overrides={
+          "diffusion_sampler": "entropy_bound",
+          "diffusion_entropy_bound": 0.1,
+      },
+      diffusion_config={"canvas_length": 256},
+  )
+
+  messages = [{"role": "user", "content": "Explain quantum computing in simple terms."}]
+  prompt = tokenizer.apply_chat_template(messages, tokenize=False, add_generation_prompt=True)
+  outputs = llm.generate(prompt, SamplingParams(temperature=0.0, max_tokens=1024))
+
+  print(outputs[0].outputs[0].text)
+  ```
+
+  ### Thinking Mode
+
+  Launch the server with `--reasoning-parser gemma4`, then enable per-request:
+
+  ```python
+  response = client.chat.completions.create(
+      model="google/diffusiongemma-26B-A4B-it",
+      messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "What is the derivative of x^3 * ln(x)?"}],
+      max_tokens=32768,
+      extra_body={"chat_template_kwargs": {"enable_thinking": True}},
+  )
+  ```
+
+  ## Performance Characteristics
+
+  Compared to the autoregressive Gemma 4 26B-A4B baseline (single H100, concurrency=1, SPEED-Bench):
+
+  | Metric | Gemma 4 26B-A4B (baseline) | DiffusionGemma 26B-A4B |
+  |--------|---------------------------|------------------------|
+  | Output TPS | 199 tok/s | 375 tok/s (**1.9×**) |
+  | E2E Request Time (mean) | 2.87s | 0.88s (**3.3× faster**) |
+  | TTFT (mean) | 53ms | 489ms (higher due to canvas denoising setup) |
+  | Per-request Gen TPS (mean) | 205 tok/s | 1,282 tok/s (**6.2×**) |
+
+  The diffusion model trades higher time-to-first-token for significantly higher generation throughput. It generates fewer total tokens per prompt on average (shorter outputs) but completes requests much faster.
+
+  ## Known Limitations
+
+  - **TTFT**: ~10× higher than autoregressive baseline — the model must denoise an entire canvas block before emitting the first token.
+  - **`--max-num-seqs`**: Must be kept low (≤4) due to the large diffusion state tensors. Higher values cause CUDA OOM.
+  - **Audio**: Not supported — the diffusion checkpoints do not include an audio encoder.
+  - **Function Calling**: Works best in thinking mode. Non-thinking mode may answer directly instead of emitting tool calls.
+
+  ## References
+
+  - [Model card](https://huggingface.co/google/diffusiongemma-26B-A4B-it)
+  - [vLLM structured-read support for DiffusionGemma](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57250)
+  - [djev-run Cloud Run deployment](https://github.com/taeold/djev-run)
+  - [Gemma 4 26B-A4B (autoregressive baseline)](https://huggingface.co/google/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it)
+  - [Gemma docs](https://ai.google.dev/gemma/docs)

+guide: |
+  ## Overview
+
+  [Gemma 4](https://ai.google.dev/gemma/docs) is Google's most capable open model family, featuring a unified multimodal architecture that natively processes text, images, and audio. The **12B Unified** model is *encoder-free*: instead of dedicated vision/audio encoders, it projects raw image patches and audio waveforms directly into the decoder's embedding space through lightweight linear layers, so every modality flows into a single decoder-only transformer. Gemma 4 models support structured thinking/reasoning, function calling with a custom tool-use protocol, and dynamic vision resolution — all available through vLLM's OpenAI-compatible API.
+
+  ### Key Features
+  - **Encoder-free multimodality**: Text, image, and audio inputs handled by a single decoder-only transformer — no separate encoders to load, reducing multimodal latency.
+  - **Dual Attention**: Alternating sliding-window (local, 1024 tokens) and global attention; the final layer is always global, with unified Keys/Values and Proportional RoPE on global layers for long-context efficiency.
+  - **Thinking Mode**: Structured reasoning via `<|channel>thought\n...<channel|>` delimiters.
+  - **Function Calling**: Custom tool-call protocol with dedicated special tokens.
+  - **Native System Prompt Support**: First-class `system` role.
+
+  ### Supported Variants
+
+  Dense:
+  - `google/gemma-4-E2B-it` (effective 2B)
+  - `google/gemma-4-E4B-it` (effective 4B)
+  - `google/gemma-4-12B-it` (11.95B, encoder-free)
+  - `google/gemma-4-31B-it` (31B)
+
+  MoE:
+  - `google/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it` (26B total / 4B active)
+
+  > **Context length**: this recipe pins `context_length` to the value in `config.json` (`max_position_embeddings = 131072`, i.e. 128K). The Gemma 4 model card markets the 12B at up to 256K — raise `--max-model-len` only if your vLLM build accepts it.
+
+  TPU support is provided through [vLLM TPU](https://github.com/vllm-project/tpu-inference) with recipes for [Trillium](https://github.com/AI-Hypercomputer/tpu-recipes/tree/main/inference/trillium/vLLM/Gemma4) and [Ironwood](https://github.com/AI-Hypercomputer/tpu-recipes/blob/main/inference/ironwood/vLLM/Gemma4/).
+
+  > **Nightly required**: support for the encoder-free 12B Unified model landed in [vllm-project/vllm#44429](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/44429) and has not yet shipped in a stable release. Use the pinned Docker image (recommended) or a nightly pip wheel.
+
+  ## Prerequisites

+      model="google/gemma-4-12B-it",
+      messages=[{"role": "user", "content": [
+          {"type": "image_url", "image_url": {"url": "https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/3a/Cat03.jpg/1200px-Cat03.jpg"}},
+          {"type": "text", "text": "Describe this image in detail."},
+      ]}],
+      max_tokens=1024,
+  )
+  ```
+
+  ### Audio
+  Requires `uv pip install "vllm[audio]"`.
+  ```bash
+  vllm serve google/gemma-4-12B-it \
+    --max-model-len 8192 \
+    --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image": 4, "audio": 1}'
+  ```
+
+  ### Thinking Mode
+  ```bash
+  vllm serve google/gemma-4-12B-it \
+    --max-model-len 16384 \
+    --enable-auto-tool-choice \
+    --reasoning-parser gemma4 \
+    --tool-call-parser gemma4 \
+    --chat-template examples/tool_chat_template_gemma4.jinja
+  ```
+  Enable thinking per-request via `extra_body={"chat_template_kwargs": {"enable_thinking": True}}`, or default-on with `--default-chat-template-kwargs '{"enable_thinking": true}'`.
+
+  ### Structured Outputs
+  vLLM guided decoding constrains output to a JSON schema. Include semantic instructions in the system prompt — the model does not see schema descriptions.
+
+  ## Configuration Tips
+
+  - Set `--max-model-len` to match your workload.
+  - `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.90–0.95` maximizes KV cache.
+  - Image-only workloads: pass `--limit-mm-per-prompt.audio 0`.
+  - Text-only workloads: pass `--limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image": 0, "audio": 0}'` to skip MM profiling.
+  - `--async-scheduling` improves throughput.
+  - FP8 KV cache (`--kv-cache-dtype fp8`) saves ~50% KV memory.
+
+  ## Speculative Decoding (MTP)
+
+  Enable the **Spec Decoding** feature toggle (above) or add `--speculative-config` manually to use MTP drafting with the [assistant model](https://huggingface.co/google/gemma-4-12B-it-assistant). Recommended `num_speculative_tokens`: 4–8 for this model.
+
+  > **Note:** MTP speculative decoding for Gemma 4 requires the nightly build — the pinned `vllm/vllm-openai:gemma4-unified` image or a nightly pip wheel. The standard `:latest` stable tag does not include this feature.
+
+  ## References
+
+  - [Model card](https://huggingface.co/google/gemma-4-12B-it)
+  - [vLLM support PR (#44429)](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/44429)
+  - [Assistant (MTP draft) model](https://huggingface.co/google/gemma-4-12B-it-assistant)

+  - [TPU recipes: Trillium](https://github.com/AI-Hypercomputer/tpu-recipes/tree/main/inference/trillium/vLLM/Gemma4)
